articles.title: ‘Other Mommy’ Star Arabella Olivia Clark on Working With Jessica Chastain and Being Mentored by Mckenna Grace
articles.summary: Arabella Olivia Clark is proud to scare you. The 10-year-old actress joined Variety over Zoom from her Los Angeles hotel room the morning after the premiere of “Other Mommy, wearing a jacket with her character’s name, Bela, printed on the front.
body: For Clark, who previously played a younger version of Amanda Seyfried’s character in the 2025 film “The Housemaid,” “Other Mommy” marks her first time leading a feature film. Clark might specialize in frightening audiences, but she’s not easily frightened herself.
“I love spiders. I love snakes. I like all the creepy stuff,” she replies when asked what scares her the most. “I love the dark, so I don’t really know what I would be afraid of.”

Clark’s open mind and adventurous spirit extend well beyond the screen. When she’s not acting, Clark takes sailing and swimming lessons — the latter of which came in handy for “Other Mommy” — and spends much of her free time reading. Before even landing the role of Bela, she read the film’s source material, Josh Malerman’s 2024 novel “Incidents Around the House,” in just three days. By her second audition, she was well prepared, though the story still managed to get under her skin. “I got chills!” she shares.

articles.title: ‘The Furious’ Star Xie Miao to Headline U.S.-Set Martial Arts Crime Thriller for Stars Collective (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Chinese martial arts star Xie Miao (“The Furious,” the “Eye for an Eye” series) is set to lead an English-language action crime thriller set in the U.S., which Los Angeles-based Stars Collective has in development.
body: “Xie Miao is the perfect artist to lead this fast-paced, adrenaline-fueled movie, with real physical requirements only a professional of his caliber can perform,” said Xu.

Born in Beijing, Xie started out as a child actor and collected multiple wushu championship titles. He broke through opposite Jet Li, with the pair cast as father and son in “The New Legend of Shaolin” and “My Father Is a Hero.”

Alongside a film career spanning decades, Xie, who holds a degree in ethnic sports, also worked on martial arts television shows. His screen work eventually landed him the lead in the “Eye for an Eye” franchise. Most recently, he headlined the action hit “The Furious.”

“Xie Miao is a powerful and distinctive action star. ‘The Furious’ showcased his appeal in hard-hitting action, and this new project will broaden the scope of the story and give his character more room, letting audiences around the world see even more of what he can do,” said Wei.

articles.title: ‘I just wasn’t going to give up’: the fight to free the longest-serving political prisoner in the US
articles.summary: Leonard Peltier was imprisoned for 49 years before his sentence was commuted. A new Netflix documentary exposes the ‘corrupt’ system that allowed it to happen. On 20 January 2025, with 14 minutes remaining in his term as president, Joe Biden commuted the life sentence of Leonard Peltier, after…
body: Outside the Florida prison where Peltier was being held that morning were several of the many activists and lawyers who fought for his release, as well as film-makers David France and Jesse Short Bull. The two directors’ long-gestating documentary on Peltier’s fight for justice was set to premiere just a week later at the Sundance film festival with a very different ending, the octogenarian still awaiting a chance to return home to the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa reservation in North Dakota. That morning, there was “a sinking feeling that it wasn’t going to happen”, France said.

When it did, while the cameras rolled, the line of supporters erupted in joy for a commutation that allowed Peltier to serve the rest of his consecutive life sentences on house arrest, though it did not pardon him – not quite justice, but a victory so uncertain and so hard-fought, over more than half a lifetime, that I have cried every time I’ve rewatched it.

articles.title: Ray Gunn review – Brad Bird’s animated film-noir sci-fi caper is an old-school family classic
articles.summary: Sam Rockwell voices the gumshoe who becomes embroiled with Scarlett Johansson’s femme fatale in this big-hearted and beautifully designed fantasy spectacular. Brad Bird, the Spielberg of animation, applies his masterly authorial touch to a terrific family film that retrieves the genre from the…
body: When Venus discovers his planned scam, she threatens to kill Arnold in front of witnesses, creating a murderous cloud over her reputation – but malevolent Arnold has something on her too. It all leads to a scary plot, involving Venus’s smoothie manager and first husband Barry (Alan Tudyk) and fez-wearing nightclub proprietor and mob boss Slugsy (Matt Berry), who comes on like a cross between Sydney Greenstreet and Jabba the Hutt.

There are some lovely set piece scenes – especially when Ray and Venus take to the floor at a club which offers a “zero gravity” interlude allowing its dancers and lovers the chance to float surreally around as if in space. We also get a bizarre interlude when a gun turns out to be – temporarily – capable of scrambling the limbs of those in its sights. And on top of all that, the film has something to say about algorithmic ads and data privacy. It’s a charming, very enjoyable movie with a big heart.

articles.title: Joseph Gordon-Levitt Says Instead of Being Afraid of AI, “We Should Be Concerned About the People Building AI”
articles.summary: "These models are being trained to hijack your intimacy, to make friends with you, to get you to fall in love with it," the actor said of technology's training.
body: Joseph Gordon-Levitt, who was appointed the United Nations’ first global advocate for human-centric digital governance in March, is arguing that instead of being afraid of AI, “we should be concerned about the people building AI.”

In a new video interview with The New York Times, the actor was asked his current biggest fear about the technology. “I would object to that question just because reducing these concerns into one sound bite of fear — that’s one of the problems,” Gordon-Levitt responded.

The Don Jon star previously opened up about his concerns about AI, arguing at a panel hosted by The Hollywood Reporter and Autodesk at Sundance that “we need to build a system for ongoing compensation” as the technology depends on “human input.”

He also joined a group of industry insiders last December to form the Creators Coalition on AI, with its mission being to provide “a central coordinating hub to upgrade our industry’s systems and institutions.” The group additionally has an advisory council that seeks “to establish shared standards, definitions and best practices as well as ethical and artistic protections for if and when AI is used in entertainment projects.”

articles.title: 5 Forgotten Netflix Fantasy TV Shows That Still Hold Up Today
articles.summary: Netflix has given us some truly ambitious and creative, yet since forgotten, fantasy series. Here are five such shows that warrant your attention.
body: Netflix has given the world a lot of good things. The streamer famously saved "Breaking Bad" from an early cancellation due to its huge rise in viewership the moment it debuted on the platform. Meanwhile, shows like "Lucifer" and "Manifest" outright came back from the dead thanks to Netflix giving them new seasons.

That being said, these days, Netflix has just so many original series and movies that the vast majority tend to, at worst, quickly disappear into the ether or, at best, enjoy some popularity for a few weeks before vanishing from our collective memory. For every "Stranger Things," there is a "Hemlock Grove," after all. Indeed, there are plenty of very good but mostly forgotten Netflix TV shows, from comedies to documentaries and animated series.

articles.title: Ava DuVernay Sounds the Alarm Over the “Erosion of Democracy” at ’14th’ World Premiere: “We Need to Fight”
articles.summary: The Netflix documentary about the significance of and challenges to the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was the closing night screening at the 2026 New York Film Festival.
body: Ava DuVernay brought the world premiere of 14th, her Netflix documentary about the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, to the closing night of the 2026 New York Film Festival.
At the premiere, DuVernay and documentary participants Stacey Abrams and Sherrilyn Ifill made it clear: The threat to the future of U.S. democracy is upon us, and it’s time to fight.
“I’m not really interested in instilling hope,” DuVernay told The Hollywood Reporter of what she hopes viewers take away from the film. Instead, she said she wanted people to “feel ignited.”
“I’m interested in stirring the fight in people,” she added. “We’ll see what happens.”

articles.title: Anime Series ‘Sentinel 6’ in Development With NBA and NFL Pros Michael Carter-Williams and Jamaal Williams as EPs
articles.summary: Influencer King Vader is among the voice cast, with LeSean Thomas of ‘Bass x Machina’ and ‘The Boondocks’ credited as the pilot writer and a consulting producer on the Afro-futurist sci-fi adventure.
body: Sentinel 6, an Afro-futurist sci-fi adventure anime, is in development with NBA and NFL Pros Michael Carter-Williams and Jamaal Williams, respectively, boarding as executive producers.

Created in 2019 by Jamaican-American writer Pat Stout and the late Bronx native Asa Palmer through their production company Sable Kudzu, Sentinel 6 is set in the year 2429, around 400 years after a near extinction-level event on Earth known as the Great Phoenix War.

A mix of Afro-Futurism, TV-MA new adult, and sci-fi action-adventure, the series will be comprised of 11 to 12 thirty-minute episodes. LeSean Thomas ( Bass x Machina, Yasuke, The Boondocks ) wrote the pilot and serves as a consulting producer on the project, with both Carter-Williams and Williams serving as executive producers, alongside independent talent manager Sam Goff, who also reps Stout via Animated Perspectives. Carter-Williams and Williams have also invested in the indie series, which, in 2024, ran a successful Kickstarter campaign raising nearly $20,000 that was used to create a trailer produced by the Bulgarian and German Chase A Cloud Studio.
